narrative.overview: SICAP.ai is a clean public ledger of where Romanian public money goes. The interface earns trust the way a good record does: by being accurate, legible, and free of anything that distracts from the facts. The data is the design; a contract code, a sum in lei, a contracting authority, a date are the protagonists, and the chrome stays quiet so they read first. It is built on a restrained Civic Blue and Slate base over near-white paper (deep slate-navy in dark mode), with color rationed to a single action accent plus a fixed three-hue code for procurement types. Surfaces are flat at rest and lift only on hover; typography splits cleanly into a grotesque for language and its monospace twin for every number.
keyCharacteristics: Data-forward: numbers, codes, and dates are set in monospace and treated as first-class content.
Rationed color: one Civic Blue accent, plus a fixed blue/amber/emerald code for the three procurement types.
Flat by default: subtle rest shadows, a gentle lift on hover, depth carried mostly by tonal slate tints.
Search-first: the query field is the hero on the home surface and never buried elsewhere.
Bilingual discipline: Romanian UI copy with diacritics intact, English code.

rules.name: The Civic Blue Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent. Civic Blue appears on roughly a tenth of any screen: actions, links, focus, brand. Its scarcity is what makes a blue word obviously clickable. Do not introduce a second decorative accent.

rules.name: The Type-Coding Rule
rules.body: Blue means direct, amber means offline, emerald means public. Always, and only. These three hues are spoken for; never reuse them for decoration or emphasis unrelated to procurement type.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Every figure that is data, a contract code, a sum, a CUI, a date, is set in Geist Mono. Prose is never monospace; data is never proportional. This single split is the most recognizable thing about the type system.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flat. A shadow heavier than shadow-sm may only appear as a response to state (hover, focus, an open popover or dialog). A card that floats at rest is wrong here.

dos: Do keep Civic Blue (#2563eb) to roughly 10% of a screen: actions, links, focus, brand.
Do set every figure (code, sum, CUI, date) in Geist Mono, and keep prose in Geist Sans.
Do signal procurement type with the fixed code: blue = direct, amber = offline, emerald = public.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest (shadow-sm) and reserve shadow-md for hover and open overlays.
Do preserve Romanian diacritics in all copy, and keep contrast and focus rings at WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes.
Do lead with the search field. It is the hero; never make a user hunt for it.
donts: Don't use a colored left-border stripe thicker than 1px as a type marker; carry type through the tinted pill and colored date numerals instead.
Don't reproduce government-portal bloat: the cluttered, slow, bureaucratic, deep-nested feel of e-licitatie.ro.
Don't drift into hypey SaaS marketing: gradient blobs, gradient text, hero-metric templates, or emoji enthusiasm.
Don't go consumer-playful: no mascots, jokey microcopy, or gamified flourishes.
Don't settle into generic AI-dashboard sameness: identical card grids, purple gradients, or decorative glassmorphism.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or spend the type-coding blue/amber/emerald on anything unrelated to procurement type.
Don't use em dashes in UI copy; prefer a spaced middot, comma, or colon.
